answer: We define a security primitive where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds impose a saffron cost on collateral to neutralize Sybil-based identity multiplication. Subgame-perfect slashing matrices act as a beacon for validator honesty by ensuring that any replicated node presence pushes the actor off the financial ledge of solvency through non-linear penalty functions. Rigorous analysis proves that the expected utility of malicious entry remains strictly negative, facilitating Nash equilibrium convergence within adversarial multi-agent environments.
